title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the last page (61/61) of a dossier that tries to attach to a motive M over a number field k a Galois representation with values in its 'Mumford–Tate'/motivic group G, with an adelic component at every place, including an archimedean one. Page 60 sets this up: there are homomorphisms phi: Gal(k/k_0) -> G(A_f) (the transcription has A_c), the image is dense, and the closure of the image is an open subgroup.

This page asks how that homomorphism depends on the auxiliary choice of a place or embedding w.

(1) Setup. For each embedding w there is an integral Betti-type lattice M_w^Z, living inside a common adelic or extended-scalar realization M_{k^{(∞)}}. An element sigma acts on that realization through an operator sigma-dot. Transport along w -> sigma w gives M_{sigma w}^Z = sigma-dot(M_w^Z). The representation attached to the base point v is written sigma_* = phi_v(sigma); it is defined by sigma-dot M_v^Z = sigma_* M_v^Z.

(2) Change of base point. Suppose M_w^Z = g M_v^Z with g in G(M_{k^{(∞)}}); Grothendieck calls w and v 'M-equivalent'. Then:
- M_{sigma w}^Z = sigma-dot g M_v^Z = (sigma-dot g sigma-dot^{-1}) sigma_* M_v^Z = (sigma-dot g sigma-dot^{-1}) sigma_* g^{-1} M_w^Z.
- Hence sigma'_* = sigma-dot g sigma-dot^{-1} sigma_* g^{-1}.

(3) Finite places. At a finite place l, sigma-dot_l = sigma_l, so sigma'_l = sigma_l g_l sigma_l^{-1} sigma_l g_l^{-1} = sigma_l. The l-adic (finite-adelic) components therefore do not depend on the choice of w within an M-equivalence class. The line after this reads 'd'où nécessairement' (not 'assainissement').

(4) Archimedean place. Here sigma-dot_inf acts semilinearly, through the action on the archimedean coefficients, and does not cancel. One gets phi_w(sigma) = g_inf^{sigma-dot} phi_v(sigma) g_inf^{-1}. This is a twisted conjugation, i.e. phi_w and phi_v differ by a coboundary in nonabelian Galois cohomology H^1(Gal, G(k^{(∞)}_inf)).

Purpose. The page settles how well defined the 'motivic Galois representation' is. Only its infinite component depends on the base point, and only up to a cohomologous cocycle. This is exactly the structure later encoded in the Taniyama group, where the finite-adelic splitting over A_f is canonical and the archimedean part carries the extension class. The same structure appears in Deligne's treatment of how Betti cohomology of X and of a Galois conjugate X^sigma are identified, adelically and via absolute Hodge cycles.
errors: Grothendieck himself flags a gap in the margin: 'N.B. il y a ici une petite vérification à faire sur w…'. The claim M_{sigma w}^Z = sigma-dot(M_w^Z), and how sigma acts on the place w, is not justified on the page.
The boxed formula writes g_inf^sigma, but the derivation gives g_inf^{sigma-dot_inf}, the twist by the archimedean action. This is a notational slip.
A first crossed-out version, phi_w(sigma) = g_inf^{sigma-dot} phi_v(sigma) g_inf, lacks the inverse; it is corrected in the boxed line.
The finite-place computation silently assumes sigma-dot_l = sigma_l, i.e. that the transport action equals the Galois action on l-adic realizations. This is plausible by definition but not stated.

ideas.what: Changing the base embedding w within an M-equivalence class changes the Galois homomorphism phi_w: Gal -> G(adeles) by a twisted conjugation (a coboundary) concentrated at the archimedean component; the l-adic components are invariant.
ideas.modern_name: Independence of l-adic components and cohomology class of the archimedean cocycle; conjugation of motives/Betti lattices (cf. Taniyama group splitting over A_f)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (absolute Hodge cycles, 1979–82); Langlands (Taniyama group, 1979); Milne–Shih (1982)

ideas.what: Comparison of Betti lattices of conjugate embeddings M_{sigma w}^Z = sigma-dot(M_w^Z) via an adelic/semilinear action.
ideas.modern_name: Galois conjugation of Betti cohomology, H_B(X^sigma) ⊗ A_f ≅ H_B(X) ⊗ A_f

ideas.what: Computation of sigma'_* = sigma-dot g sigma-dot^{-1} sigma_* g^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: change of trivialization of a nonabelian 1-cocycle

missed.claim: Together with page 60 (Galois image dense and open in G(A_f)), the page sets up a motivic Galois homomorphism into G(adeles). Its finite-adelic part is canonical (independent of the embedding up to M-equivalence), while its archimedean part is defined only up to a twisted-conjugation coboundary. This is the structural shape of the Taniyama group and of Langlands' conjugation-of-Shimura-varieties picture, apparently ca. 1969–72, before Langlands (1979) and Deligne/Milne–Shih (1982).
missed.quote: On a donc pour ℓ fini σ'_ℓ = σ_ℓ g_ℓ σ_ℓ^{-1} σ_ℓ g_ℓ^{-1} = σ_ℓ … φ_w(σ) = g_∞^σ φ_v(σ) g_∞^{-1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an early Grothendieck formulation of adelic motivic Galois representations with archimedean twisting. This is relevant to the history of the Taniyama group and of the conjugation of motives, though the page is too fragmentary to claim priority.

missed.claim: The verification 'sur w' is left undone, and the notion of 'M-équivalence' of embeddings or places is introduced but not developed.
missed.quote: N.B. il y a ici une petite vérification à faire sur w....
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor; the gap is likely routine to fill.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation itself is routine cocycle algebra. Its context — an adelic motivic Galois representation, with the archimedean place as the only source of dependence on the embedding — prefigures Taniyama-group and conjugation-of-motives ideas. But the page is fragmentary and the framework is not clearly identifiable.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'Cette' is written heavily but is probably not struck out: 'Cette application peut s'écrire si w' = σw'.
Marginal note reads 'N.B. il y a ici une petite vérification à faire sur w....'.
On the previous page, 'G(A_c)' is probably 'G(A_f)' (finite adeles).
Boxed formula: the exponent on g_∞ is σ (intended σ̇_∞).
